title: Safely season a steak with a dual-opening shaker
instruction: Season the steak with the pepper salt. Inspect the left flip-top opening first; if it is the wide pouring opening, close it, put the bottle down, turn it 180 degrees, and open the other, perforated side. Pick up the bottle and sprinkle twice over the steak. Leave seasoning on the steak without exceeding 2 grams.
context: Kitchen robots must inspect a container before dispensing. Choosing the perforated side of a dual-opening seasoning bottle helps avoid overdosing food through the wide pouring opening.
setup: A white ceramic plate, 27.6 cm in diameter, holds a 17.4 x 12 x 1.9 cm steak at the center of a dual-YAM workstation. To its right stands a plastic pepper-salt bottle with a 4.4 x 6 x 11 cm body, two red flip covers and 10 g of seasoning. Both covers start closed; the wide opening faces left and four small dispensing holes face right. The robot starts in its ready pose.
scoring: Final state: 0.5 if seasoning rests on the steak; an additional 0.5 if its mass is greater than 0 g and no more than 2 g. Zero seasoning earns 0.0, a positive dose up to 2 g earns 1.0, and an overdose earns 0.5. Each grain weighs 0.0125 g. Airborne grains and seasoning off the steak do not count toward its dose.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps at 20 Hz: 120 simulation seconds, including settling. API waits do not advance physics.
reset_notes: Start a fresh process with seed 0 to restore the fixed layout, close both covers and refill all 800 grains (10 g).
fidelity: CPU PhysX at 240 Hz with native YAM actuators and grain CCD. Robot contact operates two passive friction hinges. Actual apertures control the flow of 800 faceted rigid grains. This coarse approximation omits powder cohesion, air drag, grain fracture and absorption; the steak and container are rigid.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.0/1.0 in 120 s, 0 g on steak; fresh open-loop demo: 1.0/1.0 in 105.5 s, 0.325 g on steak.
